cand.title: Global Table Toronto: A World of Culture & Food Conference
cand.organizationName: City of Toronto / Toronto History Museums
cand.excerpt: Strong organized hospitality-demand mechanism and confirmed Toronto date; venue commitment reduces current-edition accessibility.
cand.selectionWhy: Ledger shows competitor venue/hotel: Toronto Marriott City Centre Hotel

quote.assumption: exa agent fixed effort=high (contact enrichment not included)

findings.namedBuyers: Shiralee Hudson Hill, Director, Museum and Heritage Services (Acting), is verified in a June 19, 2026 City report and personally promoted Global Table Toronto on November 5, 2026. She is the strongest named account-development/routing contact. Tristan Simpson, Manager, Museums (Acting), is verified by his professional profile and listed as Manager, Museums in the City directory: a second organizational routing contact, not a verified conference or housing buyer. Neither person is proven to control this hotel contract.
findings.futureEdition: Officially announced activity dates are October 3–5, 2027, Toronto, Ontario, Canada, within the requested horizon. These are conference dates, not article dates. Registration opens March 2027; successful presenters are notified February 2027. No subsequent edition was found officially announced.
findings.hotelProductFit: Assessment/inference using the supplied hotel specifications: a downtown city-hotel relationship is appropriate; a destination-resort pitch is not supported. Radisson Blu Toronto Downtown could plausibly serve a limited speaker/delegate lodging allocation, VIP stays or small ancillary meetings, subject to organizer demand and availability. Do not project 15–109 peak rooms as event demand: that is a product-fit range, not a published forecast. With 157 guestrooms and an approximately 240-theatre largest room, do not propose exclusive conference housing or full-event replacement without verified scale. Do not sell culinary demonstrations, tastings, receptions or catered functions until actual food-and-beverage operations and event requirements are verified.
findings.venueCommitments: Toronto Marriott City Centre Hotel is the explicitly announced 2027 conference venue. Official wording: “Located in the heart of downtown at the Toronto Marriott City Centre Hotel”. Marriott gives its address as One Blue Jays Way, Toronto, Ontario, Canada, M5V 1J4, inside Rogers Centre. This is Toronto proper, downtown in the target territory, not a suburban or resort venue. The public announcement establishes a venue commitment, not disclosure of an executed contract, exclusive housing arrangement or bedroom block.
findings.historicalRotation: The organizer describes this as a “new international conference”. No earlier editions or historical destination/venue rotation were identified. Only the 2027 Toronto edition is verified; annual recurrence, a 2028 edition and continuing Toronto hosting must not be assumed.
findings.accommodationSourcing: Published presenter policy: “All presenters will be responsible for conference registration fees as well as their own travel, accommodation and all other related expenses.” This establishes presenter responsibility for costs, not whether negotiated accommodation exists. Toronto Marriott City Centre Hotel is the only hotel named on the official event page, as the event venue. No edition-specific bedroom block, rate, booking code, housing bureau, hotel list, open accommodation RFP or appointed PCO/DMC was found. General attendee accommodation arrangements remain unknown; venue_confirmed is appropriate, not hotel_sourcing_open.
findings.organizationStructure: Municipal-government-led event: City of Toronto / Toronto History Museums, within Economic Development & Culture / Museum and Heritage Services. Not an association-owned conference despite the supplied segment label. The conference has a programming committee, but its members are not named on the event page. No external agency, PCO, DMC or accommodation buyer was identified.
findings.competitiveLimitations: The sole verified competing commitment is Toronto Marriott City Centre Hotel as the 2027 conference venue. No event-specific room block or group rate was identified there or at another hotel. Its co-located event venue creates an incumbent convenience advantage (inference), but no sellout, capacity constraint, unmet room demand or overflow requirement is evidenced. Absence of a public block is not proof that accommodation is open.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Contact Shiralee Hudson Hill at her published City email and request introduction to the 2027 conference operations/accommodation lead; use Tristan Simpson as a secondary routing contact. Acknowledge Marriott as the confirmed venue. Ask whether presenter/delegate accommodation is independently booked or covered by negotiated rates, whether supplemental hotel listings are permitted, and what measured room demand exists. Offer a small lodging-only option only after need is confirmed. Recheck the official page when registration opens in March 2027. Ask about future editions without presuming recurrence.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: For the announced 2027 edition, the main meeting venue is already selected. Do not market this as an accessible venue replacement or assume all hotel business is closed. Ancillary lodging remains unconfirmed: presenter self-funded travel/accommodation creates a possible individual-booking pathway, not a guaranteed group block. Radisson has a realistic but unproven small-scale ancillary role; there is no sourced overflow opportunity.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Conditional strategy, not verified recurring demand: develop the museum organizer relationship and ask whether the new conference will repeat, when future venue/housing decisions are made, and whether separate lodging partners are permitted. No verified future cycle, rotation or open bid supports a recurring competitive-capture classification today.
